title: Grammar: Ask one simple question (review g10 and g19)
subtitle: Unit 13: Health and services

steps.title: Ask one simple question (review g10 and g19)
steps.body: French uses avoir mal à + a body part to say that something hurts. You already know the present tense of avoir. Match à to the article before the body word.

steps.title: Use au, à la, à l' or aux
Ask one simple question (review g10 and g19)
steps.body:
• Start with j'ai mal à. Keep mal the same: J'ai mal au dos; j'ai mal à la tête.
• For le, join à + le to make au: à + le dos → au dos.
• For la, keep à la; before a vowel, use à l': à la gorge; à l'oreille.
• For a plural body word with les, use aux: à + les yeux → aux yeux.
• Use avoir for the person: j'ai mal; tu as mal; elle a mal.

steps.title: Watch out
steps.body: Say J'ai mal à la tête for a general headache. Say J'ai mal à une dent when one tooth hurts. This is only a language pattern; a health professional can help with medical questions.

steps.explain: Le dos follows au: à + le = au.
La gorge is feminine singular: use à la.
Before a vowel, à la becomes à l'.
Les yeux is plural: use aux.

steps.title: Ask one simple question (review g10 and g19)
steps.body: You can use a familiar question pattern to ask for help. In a clinic or pharmacy, vous is a polite choice when speaking to someone you do not know.

steps.prompt: You want to ask where the person has pain.
steps.explain: Où asks for the place; avoir mal is the phrase for pain.

steps.prompt: You want to ask when the pain started.
options: À quelle heure est le médecin ?

steps.prompt: You want to ask politely for help.
You want to ask politely for an appointment.
steps.explain: Je voudrais is a polite request.
